speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an infant experiencing recurrent stridor and wheezing, particularly during certain activities. To begin my assessment, can you tell me exactly what triggers these episodes and whether you are feeding via a bottle?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of stridor and wheezing worsening with neck flexion and crying, along with post-prandial vomiting, is highly suggestive of a structural issue. REQUEST IMAGES: Lateral_Neck_XRay and Barium_Swallow study. Does the vomiting occur immediately after he finishes feeding or while he is eating?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia. The clinical presentation of stridor and wheezing exacerbated by crying, feeding, and neck flexion, with relief upon neck extension, is the classic hallmark of laryngomalacia. The occasional vomiting is likely related to gastroesophageal reflux, a common comorbidity.
